title: Are Diffusion Models Vision-And-Language Reasoners?
role: Shows that only what the text adds to the noise prediction is usable for matching, the training-free case for reading d_t rather than raw predictions
reads: Conditional minus unconditional squared noise-prediction error at a noised clean image, caption as condition, t uniform on 0 to 1000, 250 or 10 noise samples per pair
trains: Zero-shot version trains nothing; HardNeg version trains LoRA on cross-attention with MS-COCO (109K) hard negatives, loss L_pos + clip(L_neg, |lambda L_pos|), lr 1e-4, lambda 1.0, batch 112, 8 epochs
combines: Image retrieval: argmin over images of E[||eps - eps(x,t,w)||^2 - ||eps - eps(x,t)||^2]; text retrieval keeps the plain error; guidance 0
adding: Subtracting the unconditional error is justified as replacing the marginal over all captions with the unconditional model (intuition, no proof); the image-side mirror with a gray image fails
noise_and_seed: Raw error depends almost entirely on the image; accuracy plateaus near 100 noise samples; 10 samples lower Flickr text retrieval from 69.8% to 55.3%; seed variance not reported
unseen: no + no held-out concepts; COCO-trained model transfers zero-shot; CLEVR colour binding 84.5% vs CLIP 53.0%, spatial 43.9% near chance
headline: Winoground text retrieval 37.5% zero-shot (chance 25%) vs 30.25% OpenCLIP ViT-L/14; image retrieval 10.2% vs 13.8% CLIP RN50x64; Stable Diffusion 2.1
suggests: (inferred) Read d_t plus the unconditional residual, since the matching score equals ||d_t||^2 - 2<r, d_t>; the same score under shared noise gives an untrained 'sum lands on joint' baseline
